key_insight: A two-dimensional chiral fluid can generate an antisymmetric "chiral pressure" that comes from a parity-breaking pseudo-scalar and remains finite even in a homogeneous steady state.
engineering_relevance: This identifies a zeroth-order constitutive effect that standard pressure models miss, which matters for CFD surrogates of micropolar, active, or chiral fluids.
method: Derived the microscopic expression for chiral pressure from the average pseudo-scalar in the fluid.
Connected the effect to rotational (vortex) viscosity in micropolar hydrodynamics.
Computed the kinetic rotational viscosity for rough disks to Gaussian order.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an analytical derivation and kinetic calculation, showing that both chiral pressure and rotational viscosity persist at zeroth order in gradients and are compatible with a steady Quiescent Chiral State.
watch_item: The result is specialized to 2D chiral/rough-disk micropolar fluids, so direct use in conventional Navier-Stokes closures may require a tailored constitutive extension.
paper_title: Microscopic origin of the chiral pressure in a two-dimensional fluid
